mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 2% in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL is increasing and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals strong economic activity and positive sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for two consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.
